messages:
maria: Quick sim run posted for Dedicated pool sizing across regions. Primary ask: decide GPU mix + autoscale headroom for next quarter. TL;DR: H100 pool 18 GPUs (sustained target), A10 pool 48 GPUs, 25% autoscale headroom recommended. charts: https://go/redwood/sizing-sims (spreadsheet + latency/throughput charts)

aj: Thanks — can you paste the key numbers here? p95/p99, and what concurrency assumptions did you use per-GPU?

maria: Sure. assumptions: baseline model is r-instruct-7b (fp16) after quantization experiments. workload: 10k rps steady with 30% diurnal spike. concurrency targets per GPU derived from continuous-batching sim. key numbers: H100: p95 ~ 42ms, p99 ~ 85ms at concurrency 10 (per GPU), throughput ~ 8 tok/ms; A10: p95 ~ 90ms, p99 ~ 170ms at concurrency 4, throughput ~ 3 tok/ms. these are median of 5 runs.

sarah-ml: Note — switching to int8 quant gave ~15% token rate increase on A10 and ~8% on H100, but increased p99 variance slightly. We included both fp16 and int8 in the spreadsheet; the H100 numbers above are fp16 baseline.

devin: Kernel choice mattered on the H100 sims — using the fused-attn kernel (v2) reduced tail by ~18ms at high seq len. Also warm-KV cache scenario vs cold changes p99 by ~30-40ms on A10.

jamal: For dedicated capacity planning we need runway for 2hr sustained unplanned burst + headroom for region failover. Maria, did you simulate a 2x burst scenario and partial region failover?

maria: yes. sim scenarios: (1) steady + 30% diurnal, (2) 2x sustained burst for 1 hour, (3) partial failover where 40% traffic shifts to secondary region. results: to meet p99 < 200ms under (2) we need +25% GPUs on top of baseline; under (3) need +40% unless we allow degraded p99 SLA. hence recommendation: baseline pool + 25% autoscale buffer + policy to fail open to hosted for extreme cases.

aj: That 25% is autoscale headroom or reserved spare?

maria: Autoscale headroom (fast spin-up from reserved warm nodes) + a small reserved hot-slab (approx 8% of capacity) for immediate bursts. we modeled cold-start penalty for new nodes as 90s to full performance, warm-slab <10s.

sarah-ml: Also factor in quant regression checks — int8 sometimes flips a small percentage of responses. If we deploy int8 for A10 pools, we should gate by eval set and have rollback in console.

devin: Ops note: if we run with aggressive batching to hit per-GPU throughput targets, tail latency increases. tradeoff chart in sheet. For Dedicated SLA I'd cap batching to keep p99 under the target.

infra-bot: Autoscale policy simulated:
```
policy: {
  scale_target: 0.75,  # target utilization before scale-out
  cooldown: 45s,
  max_scale_step: 0.25,  # fraction of pool per scale action
  reserved_warm_fraction: 0.08
}
```

jamal: Sounds reasonable. Next steps: (1) decide H100 vs mix (we recommend keeping H100 primary in NA, A10 for cheap tails in EU), (2) lock autoscale policy as above, (3) add an int8 gating eval to rollout. @aj can you own the infra rollout?

aj: I can. I'll schedule a dry run in staging and validate the warm-slab behavior. I'll also run the 2x burst test next week.

maria: Great. I'll update the spreadsheet with recommended pool counts per region and open a PR for pool definitions. Action owners: maria (pool counts + PR), aj (staging dry run + rollout plan), sarah-ml (int8 eval + regression tests), devin (kernel tuning + perf flags).

maria: One more callout — cost delta: A10-only strategy cuts cost ~40% vs H100 for same qps if we accept higher p99 (up to 220ms). Putting mixed pool allows tiered SLAs for different customer classes.

infra-bot: noted. created ticket INF-6732 with the sim artifacts and recommended policy.

aj: OK, will post results of staging test in this thread. :thumbsup:
